geometry.note: This rework is metric only. No coordinate VALUE in the tikzpicture changed except the three gloss x positions; the change of size is carried entirely by the x/y unit and the squares' minimum size.
geometry.gloss_common_x_derivation: rightmost lane right edge (5.65 units) + 4mm; 4mm = 0.4cm / 1.286 = 0.311 units; 5.65 + 0.311 = 5.961

width_verification.method: pdflatex over thesis_v2/preamble.tex, \savebox then \the\wd; \unskip applied because \input leaves the file's final newline as a 3.0pt interword space that otherwise inflates the reading
width_verification.harness: thesis_v2/_confoundmeasure.tex (reusable; define measurefile to the body .tex, then pdflatex it)
width_verification.why_not_1.44: A naive width ratio assumes the whole picture scales. It does not: the three right-hand glosses and the (a)/(b)/(c) labels are fixed-size type at \scriptsize and must not change size. Only the drawing scales, so width is affine in k, not proportional: width_pt = 148.807*k + 211.596. Solving for 403pt gives k = 1.286. Applying 1.44 would have produced roughly 425pt and overrun the block by 21pt.

compile_check.harness: thesis_v2/_confoundharness.tex (reusable; renders the figure between two full-textwidth rules)
compile_check.full_thesis_build: latexmk -pdf main.tex after splicing an input of figs/confound into Sections/03-Apparatus.tex:84 -- exit 0, 125 pages, 0 errors, 0 overfull, 3 underfull (build.sh cap is 4), 0 undefined control sequences
compile_check.audit_gate: python tools/audit.py output is byte-identical before and after the splice; the 15 failures it reports are pre-existing and concern numbers elsewhere in the document, none in this figure

known_residual: The picture's left edge is set by the 'held out' label, which is centred under the first square and so overhangs left of x=0 by 3.38pt. Centred in the block, the (a)/(b)/(c) labels therefore sit about 3mm right of the caption's left edge. v1 had the same defect at about 10mm; this rework reduces it roughly threefold but does not remove it, because removing it would mean moving the 'held out' label (structural) or letting it bleed into the left margin.
banned_terms_check: The document-wide banned term (the two-word phrase for an upper reliability bound) does not appear in this figure, its caption or this file. The figure names no estimator, so no substitute wording was needed.
